answer: Distant-witness quorums make every seat win fresh backing from strangers. Each epoch the ledger routes a seat's output through a single inlet: five established agents drawn at random, none within three hops of the seat in the payment or invite graph. Only output all five sign becomes a pearl, the unit that keeps a seat alive that epoch. A witness who signs for a later-exposed fake has its stake turned to glacier, frozen and unable to sign or earn. So each extra fake needs five unrelated honest agents to risk their standing for it, again every epoch, which no farm can buy in bulk.
